title.narrative: CEG Policy dialogue for a democratic Guatemala 2024-2025
CEG Policydialog för ett demokratiskt Guatemala 2024-2025

description.narrative:
Contribution 16855 Policy dialogue for a democratic Guatemala will support civil society in formulating proposals for democratic reforms, human rights, gender equality, and environmental protection in dialogue with members of Guatemala's congress, with the aim of supporting democratic dialogue and collaboration between congress, government, and civil society.
Objective 1: Strengthen the capacity of key state and non-state actors for the comprehensive protection of human rights defenders, especially those who promote justice, through policy proposals and legal support.
Objective 2: Strengthen the articulation and the drafting of proposals with allies in Guatemala's congress in favor of human rights, women's rights, the Escazú Agreement, and the Water Law (Ley de Agua), among other themes and issues.
Objective 3: Produce information on the political context, the justice sector, politics, and proposals against corruption and impunity.
Objective 4: Establish and consolidate a space of trust and coordination with the new 2024-2028 government for the promotion of coordinated and complementary agendas and intersectoral dialogue on human rights, security and justice, and an efficient and democratic government.

Insatsen syftar till att främja demokratiska samtal och policyutveckling rörande demokrati, mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet, rättsstatens principer och miljö i samverkan med guatemalanska kongressledamöter och civilsamhället.

The contribution aims to promote democratic conversations and policy development to promote democracy, human rights, gender equality, rule of law, and the environment in coordination with members of Guatemala's congress and civil society.

The most important component of the contribution to CEG is the Security, Justice and Human Rights Roundtable, which during more than 15 years have worked to promote a legislative agenda intended to contribute to the implementation of the Peace Accords. During the last years the Roundtable has defined a "prioritized legislative agenda" with about ten proposals developed to legislative initiatives. The Roundtable is a dialogue platform for civil society (with expertise in the themes of the table) and Congress to promote and provide technical support to legislation. The Executive and national institutions frequently participate, and sometimes also private sector actors. Many of the legislative initiatives that have been developed and promoted by the Roundtable during the years have been approved by Congress.
Examples of results 2024-2025 are the following:
The subsecretary of the Inter-American Human Rights Commission presented its preliminary report 2024 to the Roundtable to obtain input to the the final report. The Human Rights Ombud and representatives of the Executive were present at the occasion. This means a recognition of the importance of the Roundtable.
CEG supported from the perspective of civil society the development of a public policy for protection of human rights defenders that was approved in late 2025. Since the policy now is completed and approved by the Government it will hopefully improve the situation for HRDs when the implementation starts.
Together with other civil society organizations and UNICEF, CEG has contributed to a legislative reform to stop trafficking of minors in Guatemala's prisons. The law was approved by Congress in February 2025 and means an important success to stop sexual exploitation in prisons.
Women's organizations have received technical support from CEG to promote the agenda for legislative reforms concerning women's rights, and to approach members of Congress for dialogue and advocacy. One of the most important results is that the law initiative about women's economic development advanced to a second round of discussion in Congress (a third round is still pendent before approval might be relevant). The intention of the law is to give the Government legal justification to be able to promote gender equality within economic development and to direct financial resources and productive projects to women, especially women living in socioeconomic vulnerability.
CEG has elaborated a large number of analysis and studies regarding themes of interest for the international community.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
